title: Wound care when reaching is hard with arthritis and frailty (UK)
meta_title: Wound care when reaching is hard with arthritis and frailty
meta_description: Looking after cuts and wounds when arthritis makes reaching hard: basic care, getting help from community nurses, and signs of infection to report.
excerpt: Looking after cuts and wounds when arthritis makes reaching hard: basic care, getting help from community nurses, and signs of infection to report.
direct_answer: Arthritis and frailty can make it hard to reach and clean wounds, especially on the legs and feet. Clean minor cuts, cover them, and ask for help from a pharmacist, practice nurse or community nurse. Report signs of infection.
author: Louis Maxwell
reviewer_credentials: First Contact Practitioner, HCPC PH128483, CSP member
keywords: wound care, cuts, legs, feet, arthritis, frailty, community nurse, infection, UK
content:
Slow-healing wounds can be a problem with frailty.

This guide covers wound care. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Minor cuts

Clean, dry and cover.

Getting help

  • Pharmacist.
  • Practice nurse.
  • Community nurse if housebound.

Signs of infection

  • Redness spreading.
  • Heat, swelling or pus.
  • Fever.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for heavy bleeding that will not stop.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Who dresses wounds at home?

District nurses can if you are housebound.

When should I worry?

If signs of infection appear.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: Cuts and grazes

Living With Arthritis is an independent charity and is not part of Arthritis UK (formerly Versus Arthritis). Everyone's situation is different, so follow the advice of your own GP and care team. If you feel very unwell, call 999 or go to A&E. For urgent advice, contact NHS 111 (NHS 24 on 111 in Scotland; in Northern Ireland, your GP or GP out-of-hours service).
